items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Ray Drummond, who was on this recording, I was lucky enough to catch him for this

ctx.x: Who’s the first five people you call for bass players, for a gig like that?

Well these days, Ray Drummond, who was on this recording, I was lucky enough to catch him for this, Ray Drummond, Rufus Reid, Jimmy Rowser, when he can make it, Jimmy Rowser is still playing, Paul West.
That’s a name I don’t know, but I trust he must be pretty good if he’s on your A list.

items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I mean we haven’t worked together in even longer but I really need to call him up and talk to him.

ctx.x: See now that reminds me I need to talk to Ray. I haven’t talked to him in probably a year. I mean we haven’t worked together in even longer but I really need to call him up and talk to him. Because I mean there’s another precious resource, folks. And he’s still here. And the people who get to hear him the most are the Japanese because they bring him over for the Golden Fingers concerts every two years.
Right, with Junior Mance and those fellas.
